name: Archivio di Stato di Caserta

profile.address: Reggia di Caserta, Piazza Carlo di Borbone, 81100 Caserta, Italy
profile.reading:
The Archivio di Stato di Caserta is the Italian state archive for the province of Caserta, in Piazza Carlo di Borbone in Caserta, north of Naples. It is a paper records repository run by Italy's culture ministry. It is not a computing facility of any kind, and it appears in this registry only because of a specific and traceable mapping error.

The archive traces back to 1818, when it was created as the provincial archive of the historic Terra di Lavoro province. During the Fascist period it was reduced to a section of the Naples State Archive, a status it kept even after the province was reconstituted in 1945, and it took its present name and standing by presidential decree of 30 September 1963. Since 2018 its offices and reading rooms have occupied space inside the Reggia di Caserta, the eighteenth century Bourbon royal palace and UNESCO World Heritage Site, while the documents themselves remain in a private building pending restoration of the palace's Vanvitelli hemicycle, designated as the archive's permanent home in 2002. Its holdings run to about 15 linear kilometres and span the twelfth to twentieth centuries. The oldest item is a parchment sale contract from Aversa dated 1143. The organised series begin with notarial protocols from the fifteenth century, and the collections include more than 500 parchments, judicial records from the French military commission and the tribunals, the archives of the Terra di Lavoro intendancy, provincial administration records from 1861 to 1927, and extensive cartographic material.

How this became a data centre is visible in the map history. The OpenStreetMap node was created on 30 March 2018 by an Italian mapper who tagged it correctly as amenity=archive, with the name and the culture ministry as operator. A 2020 edit left that classification intact. Then on 29 January 2021 a different mapper, working through a 175 change local edit whose comment translates roughly as uploading roads and much else, removed amenity=archive and put telecom=data_center in its place. The archive tag has not come back.

That single unreviewed substitution is enough to move the building into every downstream dataset built by harvesting telecom=data_center. There is a real ambiguity that makes the mistake easy to make, because an archive is a repository and the word is used in computing as well, but the tag means a building housing computing and network equipment, and nothing here does. Counting this record as a data centre would inflate Italy's facility count with a royal palace annexe full of parchment.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-05. Removed the it.wikipedia.org citation, a banned source for this registry, and re-verified the archive history against the culture ministry page, which corrects two prior errors: founding is 1818 as the provincial archive of Terra di Lavoro, not 1812, and the ministry page does not support the 1869 Santa Maria Capua Vetere merger or the 1927 to 1945 date range as previously written, so those were dropped. Also added from the ministry page that only offices and reading rooms moved into the Reggia in 2018 while the documents remain in a private building pending restoration of the Vanvitelli hemicycle, designated permanent seat in 2002. year_opened corrected from 1812 to 1818. The important new material is the OSM provenance, which turns a vague statement that the tagging is probably wrong into a documented retag: node 5516773584 v1 2018-03-30 by Spirito Libero as amenity=archive, v2 2020-04-04 by Edward unchanged in classification, v3 2021-01-29 by Umbyone in changeset 98363042 (175 changes, iD, comment Caricamento di strade e molto altro) which deleted amenity=archive and added telecom=data_center. WebSearch quota exhausted this session.
